---
title: "Model Guide"
---


## Overview

cellclass includes a curated set of convolutional architectures suited to small
fluorescence microscopy crops (typically 50 × 50 px, 1–3 channels). The models fall into
two groups: **lightweight baselines** that train quickly and are easy to deploy, and
**pretrained transfer-learning models** that leverage ImageNet features when labelled data
is scarce.

---

## Recommended models for small cell images

### Lightweight (no pretrained weights)

These models train from scratch and are well suited to grayscale or 2-channel images
where ImageNet features are less relevant.

| Model | Key strengths | Recommended batch size | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `shufflenet2x1_0` | Fast, memory-efficient, excellent accuracy/speed trade-off | 128 | **First choice** for most cell classification tasks |
| `shufflenet2x1_5` | Slightly wider than `2x1_0`, marginal accuracy gain | 64 | Use when `2x1_0` plateaus |
| `shufflenet2x2_0` | Widest ShuffleNet, highest capacity | 32 | Use for complex multiclass problems |
| `squeezenet1_0` | Smallest model, fastest inference | 128 | Good sanity-check / baseline |
| `densenet121` | Strong regularisation via dense connections | 64 | Reliable performer across datasets |
| `densenet161` | More capacity than 121 | 32 | Diminishing returns on 50 px crops |

### Pretrained (ImageNet transfer learning)

Use `--freeze-weights` to freeze the backbone and only train the classification head.
This is beneficial when labelled data is limited (< ~500 crops per class).

| Model | Input size | Key strengths | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `efficientnetb3s` | 300 × 300 (resized automatically) | Best accuracy with pretrained features | **Recommended pretrained model** |
| `efficientnetb4s` | 380 × 380 | Highest accuracy | Slower; use when `b3s` is insufficient |

> **Note on image resizing**: EfficientNet models internally resize inputs. For 50 × 50 px
> crops this upscaling can hurt performance compared to architectures that accept any input
> size. If you have ≥ 1000 crops per class, `densenet121` often matches or exceeds
> EfficientNet.

### Attention models

The following models add spatial or channel attention modules to GoogLeNet- or
AlexNet-based backbones. They are experimental and have shown mixed results on small crops.

| Model | Description |
|---|---|
| `googlenet` / `googlenet_att` | GoogLeNet with optional spatial attention |
| `alexnet` / `alexnet_att` | AlexNet with optional spatial attention |
| `simplegooglenet` | Lightweight GoogLeNet using a subset of inception blocks |
| `simplegooglenet_att` | + spatial attention |
| `simplegooglenet_ch_att` | + channel attention |
| `simplegooglenet_ch_sp_att` | + both channel and spatial attention |

---

## Choosing a model: decision tree

```
Do you have ≥ 500 labelled crops per class?
├── Yes → Start with shufflenet2x1_0 (fast sweep) + densenet121
│         Compare on W&B; pick best.
└── No  → Use efficientnetb3s --freeze-weights
          Transfer learning compensates for small datasets.

Is inference speed critical (production deployment)?
├── Yes → shufflenet2x1_0 or squeezenet1_0
└── No  → Any of the above

Do you have > 3 classes or very similar morphologies?
└── Yes → Try densenet161 or shufflenet2x2_0 for higher capacity
```

---

## Hyperparameter guidance

### Learning rate

Always sweep at least two values: `1e-3` and `1e-4`. The plateau scheduler adapts
automatically, so a higher starting LR rarely hurts.

### Batch size

Larger batches train faster but may reduce generalisation on small datasets. Use the
recommended defaults from the table above; halve the batch size if you run out of memory.

### Data augmentation (`--flip`)

| Value | Augmentation applied |
|---|---|
| `0` | None |
| `1` | Horizontal flip only |
| `2` | Vertical flip only |
| `3` | Both horizontal and vertical flips (**recommended**) |

Cells in fluorescence images have no canonical orientation, so flipping both axes is
almost always beneficial.

### Class imbalance

By default, cellclass weights the loss function inversely proportional to class frequency.
Disable with `--no-loss-weights` if your classes are well balanced.

---

## Performance expectations (50 × 50 px, 2-class)

Based on the mitosis-RPE and ppase-screen datasets:

| Model | Typical test accuracy | Training time (per epoch, GPU) |
|---|---|---|
| `squeezenet1_0` | 88–92 % | ~5 s |
| `shufflenet2x1_0` | 92–96 % | ~8 s |
| `densenet121` | 93–96 % | ~15 s |
| `efficientnetb3s` (frozen) | 90–95 % | ~20 s |

Accuracy is highly dataset-dependent. Always evaluate on your own held-out test split.
